cases.rationale: An actual black-and-white dog stands on a textured grooming work surface. Small bottles with necks are visible on the rear counter. The tiny hanging grooming tools leave scissors (76) unclear because their paired blades and loops are not resolved securely. Pale fixtures behind the dog and along the left counter leave sink (71) unclear: a basin/faucet assembly is not securely identifiable. The grooming surface is not a dining table, and wall pictures do not establish actual people or animals. I considered each of the 75 definitions; the other listed categories have no identifiable actual object in this crop.

The close crop shows an actual dog wearing a red necktie with white heart printing; it is an identifiable tied necktie rather than a scarf. Red upholstered seating is present, but the crop does not establish whether it is an individual chair (56) or a couch (57), so both remain unclear. No person is established by the dog clothing. I considered every one of the 75 definitions; no other category object is identifiable.

A woman holds a large green toothbrush at her open mouth; the long handle and dense bristled head identify the toothbrush. Additional background humans also support person. The background register and shelving do not provide an identifiable standalone display, phone, bottle or other defined object. I explicitly considered all 75 definitions, with no unresolved category ambiguity.

The central post has a recognizable parking-meter head, and passenger cars are visible down the street. Its circular meter face is not a time-of-day clock or traffic light. The overhead parking restriction sign is not a stop sign. The building, fence and pavement supply no further defined objects. All 75 definitions were considered; there is no unresolved category ambiguity.

Two standing men and the heads of an audience are actual people. One man holds a tangible red octagonal STOP sign on a pole, with readable STOP text, satisfying the stop-sign definition despite its handheld use. Curtains and stage surfaces do not establish furniture or another defined category. Each of the 75 definitions was considered, with no unresolved category ambiguity.

This crop contains street-name signs, a turning-vehicles yield-to-pedestrians sign, a pole, buildings and sky. The pedestrian on the sign is a graphic rather than an actual person. The sign is not a STOP sign, and no traffic-signal lamp/head is visible. I explicitly considered all 75 frozen definitions and found no identifiable actual object in any category, with no unresolved category ambiguity.

A conventional oven with a visible door and range occupies the foreground. Behind the work counter are an eating table and individual dining chairs. A leafy plant grows in a visible light-colored floor pot at left, and cut flowers stand in a vase on the dining table. Small pale/orange vessel-like forms around the back tabletop are too small to distinguish a drinking cup (41) or bowl (45) reliably, so those remain unclear. The foreground cabinet worktop is not itself counted as a dining table. I considered each of the 75 definitions; no other category object is identifiable.

Two actual people sit together on a long wooden slatted bench. A tennis racket with a stringed oval head and grip rests between the man's legs. The long shared seat is a bench rather than individual chairs or an upholstered couch. Clothing and loose cloth do not identify a backpack or handbag. I explicitly considered all 75 definitions, with no unresolved category ambiguity.

A person's face, torso and hands are visible beside an open laptop with an integrated keyboard. The person holds a mobile phone with a screen and keypad; it is not a remote. The laptop screen is integrated and therefore does not count as a standalone TV/monitor. Pictures on the laptop display do not establish actual depicted objects. The support surface is a computer work surface, not an identifiable dining table. All 75 definitions were considered, with no unresolved category ambiguity.

Stemmed wine glasses hang beneath the upper-left rack. A microwave with a windowed door is beneath the wooden cupboards, and part of a white conventional range is visible at the lower right. A small cleaning bottle with a narrow neck/trigger is visible at the lower edge beneath the microwave. The white round wall device lacks a clock face and appears to be an alarm; cupboard panes are not screens, and the small shelf jars are not established drinking cups. I explicitly considered all 75 definitions, with no unresolved category ambiguity.

Actual people stand on a rail platform beside a rail tram/train. The woman carries a dark shoulder handbag at her hip with its carrying strap visible. The rail vehicle is not a road bus, and the yellow track-warning sign is not a stop sign or signal light. The right person's dark vest does not establish a backpack body. I considered all 75 definitions, with no unresolved category ambiguity.

A person's hand holds an exposed mechanical music-box mechanism, showing a pinned cylinder, comb and gears. The visible hand supports person. Mechanical gears alone do not identify a time-of-day clock, and the mechanism is not scissors or a computer input device. I explicitly considered each of the 75 definitions; no other defined object is identifiable, with no unresolved category ambiguity.
